newsitem.title: USA: Policy objective key to Fed credibility - Melzer.
newsitem.headline: Policy objective key to Fed credibility - Melzer.

text.p: Setting a clear monetary policy objective is crucial for the credibility of Federal Reserve policy, St. Louis Fed President Thomas Melzer said on Thursday.

"There has been legislation proposals that would more clearly focus on the goals of monetary policy. I think that is absolutetly essential if we want to maintain the accountability of the central bank on the one hand and maintain its independence on the other hand," Melzer said in a question-and-answer session following his address before the St. Louis Society of Financial Analysts.

Answering a question about whether monetary policy can be independent despite the increased globalization of world markets, Melzer said "the only entity that can create dollars is the U.S. central bank."
"To maintain the stable value of our currency over time, that will help support trade and will also help support ... financial flows," Melzer also said.
Turning to inflation, Melzer agreed there are anecdotal data showing "there might be some risks on the upside and there has not been any change in the central bank's response to such information."

Melzer declined to comment on current monetary policy developments. The Fed has not moved on short-term interest rates since it last cut by 25 basis points both the federal funds and the discount rates on January 31.
"Very clearly, we are focused on inflation in the long run. I don't think there is any disagreement among policy makers that this is really the key long-term goal of policy," Melzer stressed.
"We certainly have not taken our eyes off of the inflation ball," the St. Louis Fed president also stressed.
